tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session: navigated to Magento admin customer_online page, logged in earlier, closed a blocking 'Incoming Message' popup, filled filters (ID from/to, first, middle, last names, email, session/last activity ranges, type, last URL, IP), clicked Search and observed 'No records found'. Many stable element hashes were captured for the popup close, several filter inputs, the Type select and the Search button. When element hashes weren't captured for some inputs (middle name, date ranges), header-anchored XPaths were used as robust fallbacks.

Task Definition:
- Build a reusable, deterministic automation tool that: navigates to the admin Online Customers page, ensures no blocking popup blocks the filters, fills all filter fields with given inputs, clicks Search, waits for grid refresh and extracts the grid rows (id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, email, ip, session_start, last_activity, type, last_url).

Action Plan (detailed to-do):
1. Navigate to {base_url}/index.php/admin/customer_online/.
2. Wait briefly for the grid and toolbar to render.
3. Close the 'Incoming Message' popup using recorded elementHash (df76c6ce85) — deterministic step.
4. Fill ID From/To using recorded input elementHashes (39a8e4b87a and 6662425bd9).
5. Fill First/Middle/Last name inputs (first and last using recorded hashes; middle using XPath fallback if hash not recorded).
6. Fill Email input using recorded hash.
7. Fill session start and last activity range inputs using header-position XPath fallbacks (first and second inputs in respective cells).
8. Select Type option using recorded select elementHash (068ccb660c) and the user-provided value text (demo recorded 'Customer' -> 'c').
9. Fill Last URL using recorded hash.
10. Fill IP Address using the header-anchored XPath (robust to column reorder) or the CSS nth-child fallback; the demo run computed a unique match and returned xpath and css candidates.
11. Click Search using recorded elementHash (197b642689).
12. Wait for result load and extract the grid rows structured into objects.

Variable Identification (tool inputs):
- base_url: target site root for navigation.
- customer_id_from, customer_id_to: ID range filters.
- first_name, middle_name, last_name: name filters.
- email: email filter.
- ip_address: IP address filter.
- session_start_from/session_start_to, last_activity_from/last_activity_to: datetime range filters.
- type: option value for Type (demo used 'c' for Customer). Use 'c','v' or empty string.
- last_url: last URL string to filter.
- close_popup: optional flag (string) to attempt closing the popup; recorded click is executed regardless but this input documents the intent.

Step Optimization & Determinism Notes:
- Prefer elementHash deterministic interactions where the recording captured a stable elementHash (popup close, first name, last name, email, Type select, last URL, Search button, ID inputs). Those are included to avoid strict-mode selector ambiguity.
- For inputs without a recorded hash (middle name, date range inputs, IP), the tool uses header-anchored XPaths that compute the correct filter cell from the header text. This is more robust than fixed nth-child CSS when the column set may vary.
- Search/Apply action is done by clicking the recorded Search button elementHash (197b642689) to keep behavior consistent with the demo.
- The tool always executes the same sequence (no conditional branching). Empty input parameters are still sent (most sites interpret empty input as 'no filter'). This keeps the tool deterministic and simple to reuse.

Known limitations and recommendations:
- Interactive-element numeric indexes returned by the demo (e.g., 136) are environment-specific and can shift if the DOM changes. Prefer the XPath/CSS fallbacks or the recorded elementHashes over numeric indexes.
- If two-factor auth or other login flows are active in the target environment, authentication must be handled separately prior to running this tool (recording assumed an already-authenticated admin session).
- If localization changes column header text, update the header-text used in the XPath (e.g., 'IP Address') to the localized string.
- If the grid markup differs significantly (no thead/tr.filter) the XPath fallbacks should be adapted to the site structure. The included JS uniqueness-check snippets from the demo run are recommended to compute exact locator uniqueness in the live environment.

This tool is single-purpose (apply filters and extract rows) and uses the recorded stable selectors where available and robust XPaths when not.
name: magento_admin_online_customers_filter
description: Automates applying filters on Magento Admin > Customers > Online Customers grid and extracts the resulting rows. Navigates to the Online Customers admin URL, closes the incoming-message popup (if present), fills all filter fields (ID from/to, first/middle/last name, email, IP, session start range, last activity range, type, last URL), clicks Search and extracts the grid rows. Uses recorded stable element hashes where available and header-anchored XPaths as robust fallbacks.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento Admin Online Customers grid page.
Wait for the page to load and for the filter controls to render.
Close the 'Incoming Message' popup if present (recorded close control). This was required in the demo to access the filters.
Enter Customer ID 'From' value into the ID filter's first input (recorded element hash). If empty, this writes an empty string.
Enter Customer ID 'To' value into the ID filter's second input (recorded element hash).
Enter First Name filter (recorded element hash for first-name filter).
Enter Middle Name filter using header-position XPath (no stable elementHash recorded for middle name in the demo).
Enter Last Name filter (recorded element hash for last-name filter).
Enter Email filter (recorded element hash for email input).
Enter Session Start 'From' using positional XPath (first input in Session Start Time filter cell).
Enter Session Start 'To' using positional XPath (second input in Session Start filter cell).
Enter Last Activity 'From' using positional XPath (first input in Last Activity filter cell).
Enter Last Activity 'To' using positional XPath (second input in Last Activity filter cell).
Select the Type filter option (recorded elementHash points to the select). Use recorded option values (demo selected 'Customer' with value 'c').
Enter Last URL filter (recorded element hash for last-url input).
Enter IP Address filter. Uses a header-anchored XPath that computes the IP column index from the 'IP Address' header — robust fallback when no stable elementHash is available.
Click the Search button to apply filters (recorded element hash for Search).
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying the filters.
Read the current grid rows and return structured row objects. If the grid contains no rows the output will indicate an empty list.
steps.goal: Extract grid rows and capture id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, email, ip, session_start, last_activity, type, last_url

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base site URL including scheme and host. Example: "http://dockerized-magento.local"

input_schema.name: customer_id_from
input_schema.description: Customer ID to filter 'From' (enter numeric id or leave empty).

input_schema.name: customer_id_to
input_schema.description: Customer ID to filter 'To' (enter numeric id or leave empty).

input_schema.name: first_name
input_schema.description: Filter by customer's first name (partial or full).

input_schema.name: middle_name
input_schema.description: Filter by customer's middle name (partial or full).

input_schema.name: last_name
input_schema.description: Filter by customer's last name (partial or full).

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Filter by customer's email (partial or full).

input_schema.name: ip_address
input_schema.description: Filter by remote IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Example: "203.0.113.45"

input_schema.name: session_start_from
input_schema.description: Session start 'From' date/time. Use the page's date format (e.g. "MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM") or exact string expected by site.

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Type filter visible option value. Recorded value mapping: 'c' => Customer, 'v' => Visitor, '' => All/blank. Use 'c' to select Customer as in the demo.

input_schema.name: last_url
input_schema.description: Filter by the Last URL visited (partial match). Example: "/checkout/cart"

input_schema.name: close_popup
input_schema.description: If a blocking 'Incoming Message' popup is present the tool will click the recorded close control. Use 'true' to attempt to close popup; default / empty will still attempt the recorded click.
